chunks: And my father (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to me from Sa'd ibn 'Abdillah, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from 'Ali ibn Abi Hamzah, from Abi Basir, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
He recited this verse: 'Verily, We will help Our messengers and those who believe in this world and on the Day the witnesses shall stand forth.'
He said: 'Husayn ibn 'Ali (peace be upon him) is among them, yet he has not been helped yet.'
Then he said: 'By Allah, the killers of Husayn (peace be upon him) have been killed, but his blood has not been avenged yet.'

key_terms.يَوْمَ يَقُومُ الْأَشْهَادُ: on the Day the witnesses shall stand forth

ai.seo_question: What does the verse 'Verily, We will help Our messengers' say about Imam Husayn?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (a.s.) interprets the divine promise in Surah Ghafir (40:51) by identifying Imam Husayn (a.s.) as the specific believer whose help was delayed until his martyrdom, illustrating the concept of 'Nasr' (victory) occurring both in this life and the Hereafter. The narration highlights a critical theological nuance: while the killers were eventually slain, the avenging of his blood remained incomplete at the time of the report, emphasizing the ongoing nature of justice for the Ahl al-Bayt.

en.sayyid-mohsen-al-husayni-al-milani: 2. My father narrated to me from Sa’d ibn ‘Abdillāh, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ‘Isā, from Muḥammad ibn Sinān, from ‘Ali ibn Abī Ḥamzah, from Abī Basīr, who said: Abū Ja’far (Imam Bāqir (a.s.))
recited the verse, “Verily, We help Our messengers, and those who believe, in this world and on the day the witnesses shall stand forth” [40:51].
Then Imam (a.s.) said, “Ḥusain ibn ‘Ali (a.s.) is among those described in this verse who has yet to be helped!!
I swear to Allāh that the killers of Ḥusain (a.s.) were killed but his blood has not been avenged yet.”
